A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MultiFinBen and provide readable main text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices. The retained benchmark components can be matched reliably despite substantial reorganization and added evaluations.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 22 models, including results on the newly constructed PolyFiQA and OCR datasets in Table 4.

after.justification: v3 reports evaluations of 21 models in Table 3 and adds original error analyses and human OCR factuality results in Appendices I–J.

M1.justification: The benchmark-selection procedure retains the same two reference models, difficulty thresholds, largest-gap selection, and lower-performance tie-breaker. PolyFiQA inputs, answer requirements, and page-to-HTML OCR remain substantively unchanged. Additional datasets and construction explanations do not establish a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds JapaneseOCR from Japanese financial white papers and GreekOCR from Athens Stock Exchange filings. This extends evaluated OCR coverage from English and Spanish to four languages and additional document environments, increasing the benchmark from 34 to 36 datasets.

E2.justification: Qwen-VL-Max is removed from the evaluated model set. It previously scored 55.40 on TableBench in v1 Table 4, but its column and model-overview entry disappear in v3. The other 21 models are retained.

E3.justification: Each PolyFiQA dataset expands from 76 to 172 instances, while SpanishOCR changes from 13,845 to 12,819 pairs. The reported annotation acceptance threshold changes from above 8 to above 5; this establishes a documented protocol revision, without proving reruns. Appendix J introduces four-point factuality evaluation on 256 English, 50 Spanish, and 100 Greek OCR outputs.

E4.justification: New Appendix I analyzes financial-field extraction errors in GPT-4o and LLaMA3.1-70B PolyFiQA outputs and identifies five categories of GPT-4o OCR errors. Appendix J adds human factuality assessment. These provide substantial diagnostic evidence beyond the aggregate performance analyses available in v1.

E5.justification: v3 Table 8 newly reports Cohen’s kappa and Krippendorff’s alpha for OCR human evaluation. The PolyFiQA agreement percentages and Gwet’s AC1 documentation were already present in v1 and remain unchanged. No new repeated-run or confidence-interval reporting is introduced.

E6.justification: PolyFiQA results change on the expanded datasets; for example, DeepSeek-V3’s Easy score changes from 42.58 to 34.72. Japanese/Greek OCR and human factuality results are added. On the retained audio suite, GPT-4o’s average changes from 55.56 to 51.04, falling below Whisper-V3’s unchanged 51.58. Some new OCR model-column entries do not reconcile with the reported modality averages, leaving those individual attributions ambiguous.

T1.justification: v3’s new equation for mean reference-model performance formalizes the averaging procedure already described in v1. The task definitions, OCR mapping, and agreement equations retain their substance. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a multilingual, multimodal financial benchmark with difficulty-aware selection and novel PolyFiQA/OCR tasks. v3 expands the claimed OCR contribution to Japanese and Greek and updates the claimed evaluation scope. The underlying research objective and principal capability-gap claims remain stable.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving financial-field confusion and OCR omissions, hallucinations, and numeric errors, and explicitly discusses ROUGE’s limitations for factuality. It also introduces a specialization-versus-generalization interpretation and specific limitations concerning dataset scale and English-only audio. These extend substantially beyond v1’s aggregate cross-modal and cross-lingual discussion.

D1.justification: v3 adds OCR document counts and storage statistics, expands news-source documentation, describes OCR cleaning, and supplies expected reasoning steps for existing PolyFiQA questions. Reported annotation effort changes from 57 to approximately 130 hours. The evaluation harness, vLLM deployment, API temperature, and reported evaluation expenditure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Table 1 and Appendix A add FinMME and MME-Finance, distinguishing image understanding from structured document extraction. Placeholder references to earlier OCR/audio work are replaced with citations. These are limited updates within the retained research positioning; they are not additional experimentally evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten around benchmark composition, novel task families, explicit contributions, and four research questions with corresponding findings. Detailed model and task descriptions move to appendices, while limitations and societal-impact material move before the references. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: The main paper switches to two-column layout and substantially rearranges its displays. v3 adds dataset-example and construction-pipeline figures plus OCR statistics and human-evaluation tables. The results table drops language-level subtotal rows, and existing model and difficulty displays move into appendices.

improvement.justification: Expanded OCR coverage and the new error and human factuality analyses provide useful evidence that v1’s automatic scores lacked. The gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: some OCR entries conflict with modality averages, Finding 2 uses Gemma overall scores as text scores, and it claims GPT-4o audio superiority despite Whisper-V3 scoring 51.58 versus 51.04. The added diagnostic value supports a modest net improvement.
